newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria court declares Agrobusinessbank insolvent.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria court declares Agrobusinessbank insolvent.

text.p: The Plovdiv Court declared on Monday the private Agrobusinessbank (ABB) insolvent on the basis of a claim filed by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), the court said on Monday.
"The Plovdiv Court declared the private Agrobusinessbank insolvent," court official Krasimir Kolarov told reporters.
The decision is due to be written in the court's register on Thursday and the court will announce the appointed administrators to handle the bankruptcy, Kolarov said.
The BNB took over Agrobusinessbank for one dollar in December 1995 in a bid to protect depositors savings and filed an insolvency suit against the ABB a year ago.

ABB was set up four years ago by a group of private companies grouped around businessman Hristo Alexandrov, a former bartender, and Hristo Danov, both of them members of the bank's former supervisory board.
The BNB collateralised refinancing, extended to the ABB untill May 1996, totalled $11.2 million. A further $6.2 million was extended as uncollateralised foreign currency deposits, BNB figures showed.
Last October Alexandrov was arrested on charges of misappropriation and released on bail later.
Since last June the BNB has filed insolvency suits against 17 private and state-owned banks.

Agrobusinessbank is the sixth bank declared insolvent by a court. The following state banks have been declared insolvent: Mineralbank, the private Krystalbank, Private Agricultural and Investment bank, Trade and Savings bank and Slavyani bank.
Insolvency claims were withdrawn for two banks after they were bought - the Mollovbank, which was re-named Eurobank and Yambol Bank.
